hints: Notice the cylinder has height $x$ and base area $A$, so its volume is $Ax$ and its mass is density times $Ax$.
Recall that pressure $p$ equals weight divided by area $A$, and weight equals mass times $g$.
Write $p$ in terms of density, $g$ and $x$, watch $A$ cancel, then rearrange to make density the subject.
walkthrough: Volume of the cylinder is cross-sectional area times length: $V = Ax$.
If density is $\rho$, mass is $m = \rho V = \rho A x$.
Weight is $W = mg = \rho A x g$, and pressure on the surface is $p = W/A$.
Substitute $W$: $p = \rho A x g / A = \rho g x$. The area $A$ cancels.
Rearrange for density: $\rho = p/(gx)$. This is option B.

options.A: This is the reciprocal of the correct relation. Pressure $p$ increases with density, so density must be proportional to $p$, not to $1/p$.
options.B: From $p = \rho g x$, rearrangement gives $\rho = p/(gx)$, which has units of $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
options.C: Area $A$ cancels out because both weight and pressure area depend on $A$. Including $A$ in the denominator is incorrect.
options.D: Area $A$ should cancel. Pressure from a uniform column depends only on height $x$, not on total area $A$.
